item.title: Street Tree at 65 Hazelwood Lane Causing Damage to Private Driveway and Public Pavement, 1st October
item.description:
I am writing to raise an urgent concern regarding the large street tree directly outside 65 Hazelwood Lane, London, N13 5HE. The tree is now causing significant damage to both our privately owned driveway and the public pavement. Location of tree: 65 Hazelwood Lane London N13 5HE This is an issue we have raised on several occasions over a number of years. Although the tree has been cut back previously, this has not resolved the problem. The tree has continued to grow substantially and its roots are now visibly lifting and destabilising the pavement and damaging our driveway. Our driveway is privately owned and was installed at our expense, including the legitimate dropped kerb providing access to our property. We now have cracking to the driveway, movement of the paving and damage in the area immediately adjacent to the tree roots. We are increasingly concerned that continued root growth could cause further damage, including potentially affecting drainage and, in the longer term, the foundations of our property. A member of the Highways Team attended today to inspect the pavement and observed for themselves that the surface is substantially moving and creating a serious trip hazard. We were advised to contact the Council regarding the tree and the damage being caused. We are therefore asking the Council to urgently investigate the tree and its root system and, importantly, consider whether the tree should now be removed, rather than simply being pruned again. We would also ask that the Council considers what assistance can be provided towards repairing the damage already caused to our driveway, as we do not believe it is reasonable for us to be left with the cost of repairing private property that is being affected by the roots of a public street tree. There is also a significant public safety concern. We are only two doors from a primary school, and the displaced pavement is increasingly difficult for children, elderly people and those with mobility difficulties to navigate. Pedestrians are having to move around the obstruction and, in some cases, towards the road. The tree also produces substantial sap during the warmer months, creating an additional slip hazard. My mother lives at the property and is currently unwell, and this situation has made her increasingly afraid to leave the house because of the risk of slipping or falling. Photographs and video evidence are attached, clearly showing the condition of the tree, pavement and damage to our driveway. Please treat this as an urgent highways and property damage matter, rather than a routine tree-pruning request. We would appreciate confirmation that this has been logged, a reference number, and details of what action will now be taken. We have raised this issue previously and do not feel it has been adequately addressed. If we do not receive a response within a reasonable timeframe, we will escalate the matter to our local councillors for further support. We look forward to hearing from you.

Nearest address to the pin placed on the map (from OS Places API): Riverway, Southgate
Report on FixMyStreet
